root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists because the EROFS extent mapping logic classifies data as "interlaced" based solely on physical address alignment, failing to enforce the requirement that the physical length must also be block-aligned, resulting in incorrect transformation logic and out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the conditional check in `z_erofs_map_blocks_ext` from `!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)` to `!((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)`, explicitly adding a block-alignment verification for `map->m_plen` alongside the existing address check before assigning the interlaced compression format.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement checks physical address alignment but incorrectly allows classification as interlaced when physical length is NOT block-aligned. The vulnerability root cause indicates the logic fails to enforce that physical length must also be block-aligned, leading to incorrect transformation logic and out-of-bounds reads when data is misclassified as interlaced.
